claims.statement: The pinned note says shared-context Copilot pull requests use the app identity rather than a person's attribution. With repository rulesets and an existing requirement of at least one approval, it describes one additional approval before merge, enabled by default. This does not impose an extra review on zero-review repositories or prove an effective ruleset on any target.

The chat-participant fragment requires @github in prompts for VS Code, Visual Studio and JetBrains contexts while permitting omission on the GitHub website. This contextual difference must not become a universal requirement or an executed mention.

The session-opening note requires the latest editor, Copilot extension and GitHub Pull Requests extension versions in VS Code. Latest is time-dependent and unpinned; installed-version readiness was not inspected.

The cloud-agent description says it can work autonomously on issues or requests, propose changes as draft pull requests and iterate after feedback. Capability and draft creation do not establish review acceptance, merge, deployment or a currently running agent.

The comment-response fragment limits Copilot responses to repository write-access holders. It is a response authorization boundary in the embedding cloud-agent context, not proof every writer's request is safe or permission to act on untrusted comments.

The inline-completion model note says availability changes over time, a single available model yields a one-model picker, and additional or preview choices appear as available. Picker visibility alone is not a stable inventory, entitlement guarantee or model-performance certification.
